name: Beachy Head
notes: Take-off 530 ft amsl, 370 ft top-to-bottom. Large SE-facing bowl plus a shorter SSE-facing 500 ft cliff; the lower SE cliffs can be soared towards Eastbourne, and the main S–SSW cliffs past Birling Gap towards Cuckmere Haven (the Seven Sisters) in the right conditions, though there can be dangerous rotor in a SSW wind and bottom landing there is hazardous or non-existent. Lift depends on the sea being cooler than the air, not wind strength — can turn shallow and rotor-prone in summer when the Channel is still cool but the land has warmed. Cliffs must not be overflown below 200 ft (730 ft amsl) 1 Feb–1 Aug; marker flags and windsock must be flown; max 30 gliders in the air; do not overfly Whitbread Hollow Bird Sanctuary. Ample public car park, postcode BN20 7YA. Nearest A&E: Eastbourne. Airspace 5,500 ft QNH.

name: Beddugre
notes: Access & parking: From the A483 between Penybont and Llanddewi Ystradenni, turn off 2km north of Penybont towards Abbeycwmhir. Turn off at SO078698 to Cymfaerdy Farm. Ask permission from the farmer to either park at the farm or continue along the track to take off, forking left 300m past the farm (4WD only).

name: Bo Peep
notes: Take-off 600 ft amsl, 300 ft top-to-bottom. NE ridge and bowls with a long run past Firle to Beddingham Hill. The South Downs Way along the south of the top field is used by horse riders (including the landowner) — keep well clear and do not ground-handle while riders pass. Do not launch between the quarry and Firle Plantation (walk back if you bomb out there); a shoot sometimes runs in the woods below the quarry. Do not rig, launch or land in front of the public car park. Use the gated SHGC car park behind the public one (close the gate); overspill parking on the grass beside the track, watch for wide farm vehicles. Postcode BN26 6UW. Nearest A&E: Eastbourne. Airspace 5,500 ft QNH.

name: Combe Gibbet
notes:
If bottom landing; pilots should note trees, slope of field (especially in a North Westerly), proximity of road, hedges, lines and other pilots!

The site becomes rough in any wind east of north. It can be flown in such conditions but only by very experienced pilots with at least Pilot rating.

Always fly actively; on a sunny day, if you feel yourself going up, turn away from the hill into the thermal you have just found and see how far up it takes you.

Ridge soaring close to the ground can be dangerous on a thermic site such as Combe.
Rotor is reliably found within l00m of the trees beyond the west end of the site. Don't ridge soar there.

Approx elevation 270 m (886 ft) amsl. Check the site guide for temporary closures during the shooting season (Sep–Feb). No unaccompanied flying. Access through the gate next to the west side of the Gibbet (don't climb the fence). Park on the left of the track before the Gibbet, or on the right after it — clear of the gate/stiles, leaving room for emergency vehicles; don't park on the landing field. Public car park east of the road if you'd rather walk up. Nearest stations: Hungerford and Kintbury.

name: Constitution Hill
notes:
Description: A good site if you like an audience!!

Access & parking: Access is from the north side of Aberystwyth town, (Cliff Terrace). Ascend the hill by the path near the cliff railway. Or you can declare your intent to fly at the railway ticket office and try to blag a free ride to the top! Access is also possible from Clarach Bay Holiday Village to the north of Constitution Hill. Free car parking is to the S side of Clarach Village, close to the beach.

name: Cowlod
notes: Description: A smooth, grassy WSW-facing ridge with no obstructions. Ideal for low-airtimers and stress-free flying.

name: Craig y Pistyll
notes:
Description: A very rare easterly, difficult to find, hard on cars, not very high, and not very steep, awful rotor over the back, the wind comes down Pumlumon opposite, and seabreeze comes in over the back. But good fun for low airtimers and others.

Access & parking: With a map and compass you'll find it.

name: Devil's Dyke
notes: Take-off 700 ft amsl, 500 ft top-to-bottom. The club's busiest site — half-mile NW ridge to a north-facing bowl with a NE spur, then a 2-mile north ridge of bowls to Truleigh Hill; consider Firle or Ditchling when busy. The modeller's bowl (steep, wooded, right of main take-off) is for model fliers only. The paddock (earthworks to the fence west of the pub) is for hang gliders — paragliders must not inflate there if the red windsock is flying (HG present), and there's real collision risk if a PG inflates in front of a launching HG. Cows may be in the bowl; never leave gliders unattended. Slope landings not permitted for Red Ribbon pilots. National Trust pay-and-display car park (busy weekends), postcode BN1 8YL. Nearest A&E: Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton (~5 miles). Airspace 4,500 ft QNH north, 5,500 ft QNH overhead & south.

name: Disgwylfa Fawr
notes:
Description: A useful site which is frequented by the local school. Tends to work best when the wind is WNW. As such, it is a good site if Cemmaes is "blown out". Difficult to break away from due to the proximity to the sea and the sea breeze, but would have excellent XC potential otherwise. Sometimes has restitution or "magic" lift conditions on summer evenings.

Access & parking: The local school have permission from the farmer to drive further than the obvious parking place. Please don't do the same.

name: Ditchling
notes: Take-off 720 ft amsl, 550 ft top-to-bottom. North-facing bowl with a good NW take-off; ridge run 7 km east to Offham and 2 km west to the Jack & Jill windmills at Clayton, extendable via Wolstonbury Hill in thermic conditions. Good thermal site with sea-breeze-front potential. Do not launch from the small field in front of the car park; do not land in the nearby horse paddocks; beware vineyards east of the crossroads. National Trust car park at the top (charges, gate locked at dusk); an overflow option at the bottom crossroads has a poor, slippery surface and a height barrier. Postcode BN6 8RJ. Nearest A&E: Brighton or Haywards Heath. Airspace 4,500 ft QNH.

name: Elan Valley
notes:
Description: A lovely SW ridge with excellent XC potential. The westerly bowl is also flown. This site is prone to being blown out and can be reached by the sea-breeze.

Access & parking: Heading for Rhaeadr on the Aberystwyth-Rhaeadr mountain road, pass a turning for the Elan Valley lakes (this road leads to the bottom landing), go uphill for 300 yards and turn left up a steep gated track. Park on left of track and carry up the slope on the east side of the take-off. No vehicles to be taken up to take-off.

name: Ffairbourne
notes:
Description: A long NW facing cliff with great views over the estuary and potential for mountain flying. Getting away from takeoff to the first set of hills behind is not easy but can be done with persistence. Flying along the ridge towards Cadair Idris becomes progressively more difficult- the WNW sea breeze sets in but the ridge needs more of a N the further along it you go! Be careful as the windspeed in proximity to Cadair Idris may be significantly higher than at takeoff. Mind you, if you've got to Cadair Idris from Ffairbourne, you must be quite handy!

Access & parking: Please make your first visit with a Fairbourne regular and park very near to the wall by the road and don’t drive to the front of the site. No-one at all has permission to drive to the launch.

name: Ffarmers
notes:
Description: An excellent SE site, with XC distance potential limited only by the sea. Flights to Aberystwyth are achievable however. The meteo and sea breezes often meet nearby leading to the possibility of great flights in this convergence.

Access & parking: From Llanfair Clydogau follow the Sarn Helen Roman Road south-east for 3 miles gently uphill. Turn left onto stony track before cattle grid. Pass through one gate straight ahead - shut the gate (no matter how it was found). Park off the track.

name: Fforest Farm
notes:
Description: The east end of the north face of Aberedw Hill, a huge grassy ridge with room for hundreds of gliders.

Access & parking: £2 to George and Katie Barstow, Fforest Farm (SO108540); if no-one is at the farm then try the campsite (SO101534). From the A481 between Llanelwedd and Hundred House, turn off at SO103537 towards the Fforest Fields campsite. 200m past the campsite entrance fork right and follow the track to park to the quarry (SO097529). Park here (five cars maximum) and continue up the track. Follow the track to the right and and turn right again at the abandoned water tank. A maximum of two vehicles may be driven up the track to take off.

name: Firle
notes: Take-off 540 ft amsl, 320 ft top-to-bottom. North-facing bowl by the top car park, giving access to the northerly Firle ridge, the NW ridge beyond Beddingham, and the NE Bo Peep ridge. Show consideration to South Downs Way users (horses especially) and close all gates. Do not park in front of farm gates; do not launch (or land and re-launch) between Firle Plantation and the Bo Peep quarry — walk back if you bomb out there. Large public car park (paid since 2023) — beware thieves, and don't block access for farm machinery. Food/drink/toilets at Middle Farm on the A27; pub and shop in Firle village. Postcode BN8 6NA. Nearest A&E: Eastbourne or Brighton. Airspace 5,500 ft QNH.

name: Foel
notes:
Description: A grassy west-facing spur. Ideal for low airtimers and stress-free flying.

Access & parking: As for Cowlod. Then either:

name: Golden Ball
notes: XC-only, sensitive site — no ridge soaring, no pilot training or trainees, no unaccompanied flying. Approx elevation 260 m (850 ft) amsl. Pilots gather and set up at least 20 m behind take-off; max 5 wings laid out at once — 'spread the wing and go', and retreat if conditions change or you're unwilling to launch. No launches/landings beyond the fence left of take-off, and there is NO bottom landing — if you must land in an emergency, bunch up and walk back to take-off. No vehicle access beyond the Pewsey Downs public car park; use the Wiltshire Connect bus service where possible. Beware horses/inexperienced riders and always check airspace/NOTAMs.

name: High and Over
hg_rating: CP+ — not a good site for inexperienced HG pilots
notes: Take-off 250 ft amsl, 220 ft top-to-bottom. Small, steep, tree-covered E-facing bowl over the Cuckmere valley — pilots either love it or hate it, and it is not a good site for inexperienced hang glider pilots. Never fly it without a full site briefing; rig away from take-off/top-landing areas and don't block the public footpaths. Public car park two miles from Seaford, one mile south of Alfriston on the B2108 — no daytime restriction but no overnight parking; gets very busy, park considerately and don't block the road (there has been police interest in the past). Postcode BN25 3AB. Nearest A&E: Eastbourne. Airspace 5,500 ft QNH.

name: Liddington
notes: Versatile hill fort site popular for evening flights, with launchable directions from SW round to NW (treat as two separate usable faces rather than one continuous arc). Turbulence can come off the pit in the middle of the west end of the field; the bottom landing area slopes towards the road with overshoot risk, so land early. On thermic days with the wind off to the west, thermals triggering over the west of the hill fort can bring rough, lee-side air on the main ridge; the SW slope is challenging due to its small area. Access via the steel gate next to the road — close it behind you (don't use the stile/fencing at the NW corner). The hill fort enclosure is fenced by English Heritage — no flying when sheep are present and the rear gate is closed; cattle (including a bull) sometimes present too. Site closes for short periods while grazing.

name: Llanddewi Brefi
notes:
Description: A beautiful site with excellent XC potential. Sennybridge danger area is directly downwind and must be avoided to fly more than 25km.

Access & parking: From Llanddewi Brefi, take the Mountain road to Ffarmers, at the "T" junction do not take the left turn to Ffarmers, continue straight on for 400m. You'll arrive at a straight piece of road with good views of the valley below. PLEASE meet your contact there before flying.

name: Milk Hill
notes: Expansive site, diverse landing areas and strong XC potential; requires a minimum of two people present while flying, one competent in first aid acting as Site Safety Officer. Can be rough low in the back of the bowl near small trees; avoid wind directions north of west (WNW) and SSW–S due to turbulence. A single-wire electric fence in the bottom landing field is hard to see on approach — walk the field before flying. Hang gliders: a fence now crosses the L-shaped HG landing field. Access via the farm track opposite Church Road, Stanton St Bernard (£2.50 toll by QR code) to the top car park, or via the Pewsey Downs car park. Note: shown as temporarily closed following a safety incident on TVHGC's site (Aug 2026) — check the club's Telegram for current status before flying.

name: Milk Hill White Horse
notes: Popular year-round site with views of the Alton Barnes White Horse; shallow and really only works in thermic or strong-wind conditions. Turbulence from the fields in front of the hill when ridge-soaring in strong conditions; in a SE/SSE wind there's turbulence and rotor around the White Horse and the spur at the east end if flown at or below hill height. Trial rule (through end 2025, this site only): thermalling here, including the spur, is RIGHT TURN only up to 1000 ft above take-off — overcrowding on good days prompted this. Do not launch on or near the White Horse itself (lots of horses/riders nearby). Access via Milk Hill then along the path around the bowl, through the gate onto the escarpment — keep 20 m clear of the fence line for nesting birds. Public car park with a walk in from the east (pay by mobile). Note: shown as temporarily closed following a safety incident on TVHGC's site (Aug 2026) — check the club's Telegram for current status.

name: Mount Caburn
notes: Take-off 500 ft amsl, 420 ft top-to-bottom. The club's only SW site — a conical dome extending to a SW bowl. Often affected by the sea breeze, which can make the air rough; the lift band is typically small and the site can get crowded (marshalling restrictions sometimes applied). Rig on top only, not the main slope; keep take-off clear. Do not overfly the houses by the car park or south of launch, don't overfly or land in the car park, don't land in the cricket pitch or adjacent fields (use the agreed field), don't slope-land the front of the dome. SHGC car park off Ranscombe Lane is members only — no camping/overnight parking. Postcode BN8 6RP. Nearest A&E: Eastbourne or Brighton. Airspace 5,500 ft QNH (4,500 ft just north, then 2,500 ft).

name: Newhaven Cliffs
pg_rating: CP for unsupervised flying east of 'the point'; Pilot, or CP + 10 hours in the last 12 months, beyond it
notes: Low S-facing coastal cliffs — flyable when Beachy Head isn't working or Caburn is blown out; a 6.5-mile cliff run to Brighton Marina is possible in the right conditions. Take-off 180 ft amsl, 160 ft top-to-bottom. Castle Hill Nature Reserve, closely monitored by Lewes District Council — by local by-law you must be a current SHGC member to fly here. Life jacket strongly recommended. Do not fly west of 'the point' within 3 hours before / 2 hours after high water (no beach to land on, a water landing there is usually fatal — check tide tables first). Do not overfly the Park Homes site west of take-off. Postcode BN9 9DK. Nearest A&E: Brighton. Airspace 5,500 ft QNE.

name: Pen Dinas
notes: Description: A small but easy site. Wind on take off is about twice that on the beach.

name: Pennant
notes:
Description: Rarely flown- can be turbulent.

Access & parking: Quite a walk..

name: Rybury
notes: Thermally reliable XC site for experienced pilots — CP + 25 hours and completed slope-landing tasks, due to the lack of a bottom landing field. No unaccompanied flying. Landing in the col at the top of the bowl risks being blown back into rotor; if wind picks up, the shallow spur below Rybury hill fort is generally safer. Avoid flying low behind the ridge (spineback/rotor in a westerly); the spur to the north is in the lee in winds north of west, dangerous to land there. NW/NNW winds can be hazardous (max usable is WNW). Access by walking west from the Milk Hill track, through the gate alongside the fence. The farmer is concerned about unaccompanied flying — £50 penalty (to Oxfam) applies. Less experienced pilots: use Milk Hill or Sugar Hill instead.

name: Sugar Hill
notes: 1 km ridge with good XC potential, particularly in thermic conditions. Rising ground in front of the ridge limits where thermals can form, so they tend to be small and bumpy — fly cautiously. Max 5 paragliders in the air at once to prevent overcrowding. Good relationship with the landowners (family-owned) — be courteous, zero-impact, carry out all trash. Access along the marked footpath to the ridge; park in the lay-by on either side of the road.

name: Tan Hill
notes: Challenging, thermic site for CP-and-above pilots — small, so easily congested. Slope landing is difficult (undulations/obstacles); avoid landing in the east corner of the top field (rotor off the 'spine back') and watch for rotor at the west end too. Do not fly in a southerly wind — rotor off Rybury. Access via the farm track opposite Church Road, Stanton St Bernard (£2.50 toll by QR code); park at the bottom of Milk Hill near the barn, through the gate, around the field to a stile, then up — or via Rybury hill fort. SSSI — respect fences and no-landing zones; ridge soaring through to Milk Hill is possible with care.

name: Tremaen
notes:
Description: The west end of the north face of Aberedw Hill, a huge grassy ridge with room for hundreds of gliders.

Access & parking: From the A481 between Llanelwedd and Hundred House, turn off at SO081532 to Tremaen Farm. 300m past the farm turn left through a field gate marked Private Road. Park just before the next gate (SO072520) and walk up the track to take off. A maximum of two vehicles may be driven up the track to the top.

name: Uffington White Horse
notes: National Trust site (NW–NNE winds) for experienced pilots only — Pilot or Advanced Pilot rated. Beware rotor off the spur down to Dragon Hill; use the NW take-off only when the wind is west of north, the NNE take-off only when east of north. Popular with model-glider flyers — be friendly, they have equal right to fly there. Turbulence off Dragon Hill on approach to the bottom landing field. Closed on Bank Holiday weekends and every weekend through the school summer holidays. Park only in the official National Trust car park; land back at launch or bottom-land in the campsite field — no slope landing elsewhere.

name: White Hill
notes: Scenic but technically complex site near RAF Odiham, for Pilot-rated flyers only. Many trees/tree-lined areas — hazard when getting low, and rotor off the trees. Shared with model-glider flyers, picnickers, horse riders, walkers and joggers — stay aware. The B3051 below the site needs caution; make early landing decisions. No flying while horses are present, typically Wed and Sat mornings until ~10:30am (can vary). Do not fly over Freemantle Park Down (the northerly continuation) — horses in the fields below. Max 5 wings in the air at once. No vehicle access beyond the public car park; footpath NE from the car park, fence on your right.
